assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defect-mediated two-dimensional melting and the hexatic phase is a clean, universal mechanism: unbinding of dislocations and then disclinations gives a two-step melting with an intermediate phase carrying quasi-long-range orientational order. It is analytically tractable, rests on topological defects and symmetry breaking, and has shaped soft matter, colloids, thin films and the study of correlated systems. This is the kind of simple, general model I value, and it extends the line recognised in 2016 for topological phase transitions.
assessment.attribution: The theory is usually credited to Halperin and Nelson, with Young's independent and closely related contribution; the foundation of the defect-unbinding picture is Kosterlitz and Thouless, who are already laureates. Whether the three-person credit is fair to all contributors is a real question, and I am recalling the historical details from memory rather than verifying them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over decades by colloid, liquid-crystal, and simulation studies, with ongoing debate about first-order versus continuous melting in some systems. The ideas are stable and long established, so recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Experimental evidence for the hexatic phase is system-dependent, and some melting transitions are first order, so the universality of the scenario is qualified.
Overlap with the 2016 prize may lead colleagues to see the topic as already recognised.
Priority and weight among the three proposed names is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level combine Katori's magic-wavelength proposal with Ye's demonstration of extreme coherence and systematic control. They give the most precise measurements ever made, test fundamental physics and relativity, and underpin a coming redefinition of the second. The idea is simple and general: trap atoms where the light shift cancels.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the strontium clock to record precision, so a two-person prize is natural. Contributions from other clock groups, and the earlier work already recognised by the 2005 and 2012 prizes, are acknowledged but do not displace these two.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce clock performance, and international comparisons are in progress. The redefinition of the second is pending, so timing is good but not yet capped by that event.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel committee would want to wait for the redefinition of the SI second.
Overlap in credit with other clock groups (for example ion clocks) that I recall but cannot verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that cellular compartments form by liquid-liquid phase separation, with a physical theory of active droplets, brought polymer and statistical physics into cell biology. It is a surprising mechanism that is quantitatively analysable (surface tension, nucleation, coarsening, non-equilibrium driving) and has reorganised how cell biology is understood. This is close to my own interest in transferable statistical-physics concepts.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids; Jülicher contributed the theoretical framework for active droplets. The supplied credit supports a fair three-person configuration, though the fraction that is physics rather than biology and the role of other theorists and cell biologists is open.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in many systems, but the physiological relevance of condensates is still debated, and the field is only about fifteen years old. Recognition may be somewhat early and may fit chemistry or medicine as well as physics.
uncertainties: Question of whether this is a physics or a chemistry/physiology prize.
Debate on how generally in vivo structures are truly liquid phases.
Credit distribution between experimentalists and theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators, from the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect to the experimental realisation of quantized edge transport, opened a field in which band topology produces robust observable physics. The idea is conceptually deep, general, and has had wide influence on materials and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane's theory and Molenkamp's HgTe observation are well matched; Xue's quantum anomalous Hall realisation completes a coherent triple. Other key contributors (Mele, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Hasan, Haldane) leave real credit questions, and I am relying on memory for details.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and materials; the field is mature. The Nobel in 2016 covered topological phases, so this sits within an already recognised area but is a distinct discovery.
uncertainties: Competing attribution claims on theory (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Mele, Zhang) and on the 3D case (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Roy).
Technological payoff is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message passing applied to random constraint-satisfaction problems link the statistical physics of disordered systems to computational complexity, explaining the phase structure of satisfiability and yielding survey-propagation algorithms. It illustrates how replica and cavity ideas give a mechanism for why problems are hard, in line with my view of physics in computation and learning.
assessment.attribution: Mézard and Zecchina are the central names for the application to constraint satisfaction; the underlying cavity and replica machinery belongs to Parisi and collaborators, already recognised in 2021. A prize here must be precise about what is new beyond that.
assessment.maturity: Mathematically supported in part (rigorous work on satisfiability thresholds) and used across inference and learning, but its impact is mostly theoretical and the headline algorithms have limited practical dominance.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 prize to Parisi, which may make the novel contribution seem incremental.
Fraction of the results rigorously established versus argued heuristically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson required building ATLAS and CMS, among the most complex instruments ever made, and confirmed the last missing piece of the Standard Model. The significance is beyond doubt, but the 2013 prize already recognised the theoretical prediction.
assessment.attribution: Credit to the founding spokespersons and conceivers is plausible, but the discovery was made by thousands of collaborators, and the Nobel statutes limit the prize to three people. Choosing among spokespersons, detector designers and analysts is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent coupling measurements. Timing is mature, perhaps late.
uncertainties: Whether a fair three-person allocation exists for a collaboration of thousands.
Whether the committee wants to honour experiment after the 2013 theory prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realisation of strongly interacting Fermi gases and the BEC-BCS crossover gave a tunable, clean quantum many-body system that bridges Cooper pairing and molecular condensation. It provides an experimental testbed for universality (unitary gas) and pairing physics relevant to nuclear matter and neutron stars.
assessment.attribution: Grimm, Salomon and Thomas (with Jin, Ketterle and others in related work) all made decisive contributions; Deborah Jin's death complicates the picture and I do not know if this credit list is complete. The supplied three names form a plausible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple groups, with precise equation-of-state measurements. Mature, though it follows the 2001 and 1997 cold-atom prizes.
uncertainties: Unfair omission of the late Deborah Jin or other key contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned the moire flat band prediction into an experimental platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity, opening a very active field of tunable quantum matter. The mechanism is simple and general: interference of lattice scales gives flat bands.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting states. This is a natural split between theory and experiment, though other groups also contributed (for example Dean, Efetov, Young).
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely, but the origin of the superconductivity is still not understood, and the field is only seven or eight years old. Recognition may be premature compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism for the superconductivity is unresolved.
Several other experimental groups contributed key observations.
